extracted.intended_audience: PPG/NFAC administrative staff and CIA decision-makers (agency managers considering parking fee policy)
extracted.subtask_description: Internal agency memorandum evaluating the impact of instituting employee parking fees and recommending exemptions for certain classes of staff (night/irregular shifts, mission-critical drivers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess burden of parking fees on shift workers
rubrics_metrics.description: Parking fees, if instituted, will place a heavy burden on many PPG employees. PPG operates six days a week., twenty-four hours a day. Employees who work the second and third shifts literally have no means to get to the Agency except by car.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or proposing parking fees, explicitly assess impacts on continuous-operation staff and those on nonstandard shifts who lack public-transport alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider geographic dispersion and carpool feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: PPG night personnel or those who work irregular hours live in widely scattered areas in the metropolitan area. Car pools are all but impossible to form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy decisions should account for employees' residential dispersion and the practical infeasibility of forming car pools for some work schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for exceptional early/variable duty times (e.g., PDB delivery)
rubrics_metrics.description: For example, the PPG Registry's normal work day commences at 0500, and members of the Section participate in this early shift on an alternating basis. In addition, when the President is away from Washington, the Registry is responsible for delivering the PDB to the White House for transmittal to him wherever he may be. Delivery times vary. Currently, members of the Registry are reporting for duty at 0400 to provide this service. Hours such as these are not conducive to the formation of car pools nor to taking public transportation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify mission-critical functions with atypical hours and factor their transportation constraints into parking fee policy (e.g., early-morning/unpredictable delivery duties).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exempt employees required to drive alone due to job duties
rubrics_metrics.description: In many instances job requirements are such that an individual cannot be in a car pool and must drive alone. I do not feel that a person should be penalized by having to pay full parking costs because he or she is carrying out a job assignment, especially after normal duty hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create exemption criteria for employees whose job assignments make carpooling impossible or unsafe; avoid imposing full parking fees on such employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance incentives with exemptions — encourage carpooling and transit
rubrics_metrics.description: I agree that we should encourage car pools and the use of public transportation. I believe, however, that employees who work at night or have irregular hours should be exempted from parking fees or pay, at most, only nominal fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt policy that incentivizes carpooling/public transit while providing exemptions or nominal charges for night and irregular-hour workers who cannot reasonably use those alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider operational/mission impacts before instituting fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Parking fees, if instituted, will place a heavy burden on many PPG employees... (context: PPG operates 24/7 and performs time-sensitive duties such as PDB delivery).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before implementing parking fees, evaluate how fees would affect service delivery and mission-essential tasks; use operational examples (e.g., PDB delivery) to inform exemptions or mitigations.
